cards.front: What is a lingual thyroid, and why does it matter before surgery?
cards.back: Thyroid tissue that never descended from the **foramen cecum**: a mass at the **base of the tongue**, the most common ectopic site. It may be the **only functioning thyroid tissue**, so confirm a normal gland before removal.
cards.back_pt: Tecido tireoidiano que não desceu a partir do **forame cego**: uma massa na **base da língua**, o local ectópico mais comum. Pode ser o **único tecido tireoidiano funcionante**, então confirme uma tireoide normal antes da remoção.

cards.front: Which pharyngeal pouches give rise to the parathyroid glands?
cards.back: **Inferior parathyroids**: **3rd pouch**, together with the **thymus**. **Superior parathyroids**: **4th pouch**. The 3rd-pouch glands travel farther down with the thymus, so an ectopic inferior gland may sit in the **anterior mediastinum**.
cards.back_pt: **Paratireoides inferiores**: **3ª bolsa**, junto com o **timo**. **Paratireoides superiores**: **4ª bolsa**. As glândulas da 3ª bolsa descem mais junto com o timo, então uma paratireoide inferior ectópica pode ficar no **mediastino anterior**.

cards.front: What are the embryologic origins of the anterior and posterior pituitary?
cards.back: **Anterior pituitary** (adenohypophysis): **Rathke pouch**, an upgrowth of **oral (surface) ectoderm** from the roof of the primitive mouth. **Posterior pituitary** (neurohypophysis): **neuroectoderm**, a downgrowth of the diencephalon floor (infundibulum).
cards.back_pt: **Adeno-hipófise** (hipófise anterior): **bolsa de Rathke**, uma evaginação do **ectoderma oral (superficial)** do teto da boca primitiva. **Neuro-hipófise** (hipófise posterior): **neuroectoderma**, uma projeção do assoalho do diencéfalo (infundíbulo).

cards.front: What are the embryologic origins of the adrenal cortex and the adrenal medulla?
cards.back: **Cortex**: **mesoderm** (coelomic epithelium). **Medulla**: **neural crest** cells that become **chromaffin cells**. They act like postganglionic sympathetic neurons: preganglionic sympathetic fibers stimulate them through **nicotinic** receptors to release catecholamines.
cards.back_pt: **Córtex**: **mesoderma** (epitélio celômico). **Medula**: células da **crista neural** que se tornam **células cromafins**. Elas funcionam como neurônios simpáticos pós-ganglionares: fibras simpáticas pré-ganglionares as estimulam por receptores **nicotínicos** a liberar catecolaminas.

cards.front: Which hormone does each zone of the adrenal cortex make, from outside to inside?
cards.back: **G-F-R** ("salt, sugar, sex"): **zona glomerulosa** → **aldosterone**; **zona fasciculata** → **cortisol**; **zona reticularis** → **androgens** (DHEA). The **medulla**, in the center, makes mainly **epinephrine**.
cards.back_pt: **G-F-R** (*salt, sugar, sex*: sal, açúcar, sexo): **zona glomerulosa** → **aldosterona**; **zona fasciculada** → **cortisol**; **zona reticular** → **andrógenos** (DHEA). A **medula**, no centro, produz principalmente **epinefrina**.

cards.front: Which hormone does each pancreatic islet cell type secrete?
cards.back: **Alpha cells** → **glucagon** (mostly at the islet periphery). **Beta cells** → **insulin** (the most numerous, mostly in the center). **Delta cells** → **somatostatin**. **PP cells** → **pancreatic polypeptide**.
cards.back_pt: **Células alfa** → **glucagon** (principalmente na periferia da ilhota). **Células beta** → **insulina** (as mais numerosas, principalmente no centro). **Células delta** → **somatostatina**. **Células PP** → **polipeptídeo pancreático**.

cards.front: Where do thyroid parafollicular (C) cells come from, and what do they secrete?
cards.back: **Neural crest** cells that reach the thyroid through the **ultimobranchial body** (4th pouch). They lie between the follicles and secrete **calcitonin**, which lowers blood calcium. Their tumor is **medullary thyroid carcinoma**.
cards.back_pt: Células da **crista neural** que chegam à tireoide pelo **corpo ultimobranquial** (4ª bolsa). Ficam entre os folículos e secretam **calcitonina**, que reduz o cálcio sérico. O tumor dessas células é o **carcinoma medular de tireoide**.

cards.front: Which nerve runs with the superior thyroid artery, and what happens if it is cut during thyroid surgery?
cards.back: The **external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve**. It supplies the **cricothyroid** muscle, which tenses the vocal cords. Injury causes **voice fatigue** and loss of **high-pitched voice**, but the vocal cords still move normally.
cards.back_pt: O **ramo externo do nervo laríngeo superior**. Ele inerva o músculo **cricotireóideo**, que tensiona as pregas vocais. A lesão causa **fadiga vocal** e perda da **voz aguda**, mas as pregas vocais continuam se movendo normalmente.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the clinic because of a painless lump in the front of his neck. It has been present for several months and became slightly larger during a recent cold. Exam shows a smooth, round, 2-cm mass in the midline, just below the hyoid bone. The mass moves upward when he swallows and when he protrudes his tongue. There are no other neck masses. Thyroid function tests are normal. Which structure is the most likely origin of this mass?
choices: Remnant of the second pharyngeal cleft
Dilated lymphatic channels of the neck
Ectoderm trapped along a line of embryonic fusion
Remnant of the third pharyngeal pouch
questions.explanation: A midline neck mass that rises with swallowing and **tongue protrusion** is a **thyroglossal duct cyst**. The thyroid starts at the **foramen cecum** and descends through the thyroglossal duct, and a persistent duct stays attached to the tongue base and the hyoid bone. A **second pharyngeal cleft cyst** is the tempting answer, but it lies **laterally**, along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, and does not move with the tongue. A dermoid cyst can be midline, but it does not rise with tongue protrusion.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma massa cervical na linha média que sobe com a deglutição e com a **protrusão da língua** é um **cisto do ducto tireoglosso**. A tireoide começa no **forame cego** e desce pelo ducto tireoglosso; um ducto persistente continua ligado à base da língua e ao osso hioide. O **cisto da segunda fenda faríngea** é a resposta mais tentadora, mas fica **lateral**, na borda anterior do esternocleidomastóideo, e não se move com a língua. O cisto dermoide pode ser mediano, mas não sobe com a protrusão da língua.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman has a total thyroidectomy for papillary thyroid carcinoma. The next day, her voice is hoarse and breathy. She has no stridor and breathes comfortably. Her serum calcium is normal. Laryngoscopy shows that the left vocal cord does not move and rests near the midline. Injury to which nerve best explains these findings?
choices: External branch of the left superior laryngeal nerve
Internal branch of the left superior laryngeal nerve
questions.explanation: The **recurrent laryngeal nerve** supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid, so injury paralyzes the vocal cord and causes **hoarseness**. It runs in the tracheoesophageal groove and passes close to the **inferior thyroid artery**, where it is at risk when that artery is ligated. The **external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve** is the tempting answer: it runs with the superior thyroid artery, but it supplies only the cricothyroid, so injury makes it hard to reach high notes while the cord still moves. Injury to both recurrent nerves can cause stridor and airway obstruction.
questions.explanation_pt: O **nervo laríngeo recorrente** inerva todos os músculos intrínsecos da laringe, exceto o cricotireóideo; por isso sua lesão paralisa a prega vocal e causa **rouquidão**. Ele corre no sulco traqueoesofágico e passa perto da **artéria tireóidea inferior**, onde fica em risco quando essa artéria é ligada. O **ramo externo do nervo laríngeo superior** é a resposta mais tentadora: ele acompanha a artéria tireóidea superior, mas inerva só o cricotireóideo, então a lesão dificulta alcançar tons agudos, e a prega continua se movendo. A lesão dos dois nervos recorrentes pode causar estridor e obstrução da via aérea.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has taken high-dose oral prednisone for 2 years for an autoimmune disease. He stops it suddenly on his own. One week later, he has fatigue, nausea and dizziness when he stands up. Blood pressure is 98/62 mm Hg. Serum sodium is 134 mEq/L and potassium is 4.2 mEq/L. Morning cortisol and ACTH are both low. Preserved function of which structure best explains his normal serum potassium?
questions.explanation: Long-term glucocorticoids suppress **ACTH**, so the ACTH-dependent **zona fasciculata** and **zona reticularis** atrophy. This is **central adrenal insufficiency** from suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis (low CRH and ACTH). The **zona glomerulosa** is driven mainly by **angiotensin II** and **potassium**, not by ACTH, so aldosterone and serum potassium stay normal. The zona fasciculata is the tempting answer because it makes cortisol, but it is the zone that has atrophied here.
questions.explanation_pt: O uso prolongado de glicocorticoides suprime o **ACTH**, e as zonas dependentes de ACTH, **fasciculada** e **reticular**, atrofiam. Isso é **insuficiência adrenal central** por supressão do eixo hipotálamo-hipófise (CRH e ACTH baixos). A **zona glomerulosa** é estimulada principalmente pela **angiotensina II** e pelo **potássio**, e não pelo ACTH, então a aldosterona e o potássio sérico ficam normais. A zona fasciculada é a resposta mais tentadora porque produz cortisol, mas é justamente a zona que atrofiou aqui.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl has had morning headaches for 6 months. Her parents say she often bumps into door frames. Her height has fallen from the 50th to the 10th percentile. Visual field testing shows loss of the outer (temporal) half of the visual field in both eyes. MRI shows a suprasellar mass with cystic parts and calcifications. At surgery, the cyst contains thick, dark fluid with cholesterol crystals. This tumor arises from remnants of which embryonic structure?
choices: Endoderm of the third pharyngeal pouch
questions.explanation: This is a **craniopharyngioma**: a cystic, calcified suprasellar tumor of childhood. It compresses the **optic chiasm** (**bitemporal hemianopia**) and the pituitary (slow growth). It arises from remnants of **Rathke pouch**, which is **oral ectoderm**. The **infundibulum** is the tempting answer because it is also part of the pituitary, but it forms the posterior pituitary from neuroectoderm; notochord remnants form a **chordoma**.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de um **craniofaringioma**: tumor suprasselar cístico e calcificado da infância. Ele comprime o **quiasma óptico** (**hemianopsia bitemporal**) e a hipófise (déficit de crescimento). Origina-se de restos da **bolsa de Rathke**, que é **ectoderma oral**. O **infundíbulo** é a resposta mais tentadora por também fazer parte da hipófise, mas forma a neuro-hipófise a partir do neuroectoderma; restos da notocorda formam o **cordoma**.

notes.title: Endocrine glands: development, histology and surgical anatomy
notes.body_md:
## Thyroid

- Starts at the **foramen cecum** (base of the tongue) and descends through the **thyroglossal duct**.
- **Thyroglossal duct cyst**: midline neck mass that moves with swallowing and **tongue protrusion**.
- **Lingual thyroid**: tissue that never descended; it may be the only thyroid tissue.
- **Follicular cells** surround **colloid**, which stores thyroglobulin. An active gland has taller cells and less colloid.
- **Parafollicular (C) cells**: neural crest origin; secrete **calcitonin**.

## Parathyroid

- **Inferior** glands: **3rd pouch** (with the thymus). **Superior** glands: **4th pouch**.
- **Chief cells** make **PTH**. **Oxyphil cells** are larger, pink, full of mitochondria, and increase with age.

## Pituitary

- **Anterior**: **Rathke pouch** (oral ectoderm). Remnants can form a **craniopharyngioma**.
- **Posterior**: **neuroectoderm** (infundibulum); stores ADH and oxytocin made in the hypothalamus.

## Adrenal

- **Cortex**: mesoderm. **Medulla**: neural crest (**chromaffin cells**).
- From outside in: **glomerulosa** (aldosterone), **fasciculata** (cortisol), **reticularis** (androgens).
- Glomerulosa responds mainly to **angiotensin II** and **potassium**; fasciculata and reticularis depend on **ACTH**.
- Cortisol reaches the medulla through local portal flow and helps it make **epinephrine**.
- Veins: the **right** adrenal vein drains straight into the **IVC**; the **left** drains into the **left renal vein**.

## Endocrine pancreas

- **Alpha**: glucagon. **Beta**: insulin (most numerous). **Delta**: somatostatin. **PP cells**: pancreatic polypeptide.

## Thyroid surgery

- **Recurrent laryngeal nerve**: near the **inferior thyroid artery**; injury causes **hoarseness** and an immobile vocal cord.
- **External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve**: runs with the **superior thyroid artery**; injury weakens the **cricothyroid** and high-pitched voice.
- Removing or devascularizing the parathyroids can cause **hypocalcemia**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Tireoide

- Começa no **forame cego** (base da língua) e desce pelo **ducto tireoglosso**.
- **Cisto do ducto tireoglosso**: massa cervical mediana que se move com a deglutição e com a **protrusão da língua**.
- **Tireoide lingual**: tecido que não desceu; pode ser o único tecido tireoidiano.
- As **células foliculares** envolvem o **coloide**, que armazena a tireoglobulina. Uma glândula ativa tem células mais altas e menos coloide.
- **Células parafoliculares (C)**: origem na crista neural; secretam **calcitonina**.

## Paratireoide

- Glândulas **inferiores**: **3ª bolsa** (com o timo). Glândulas **superiores**: **4ª bolsa**.
- As **células principais** produzem **PTH**. As **células oxífilas** são maiores, rosadas, ricas em mitocôndrias, e aumentam com a idade.

## Hipófise

- **Anterior**: **bolsa de Rathke** (ectoderma oral). Seus restos podem formar um **craniofaringioma**.
- **Posterior**: **neuroectoderma** (infundíbulo); armazena ADH e ocitocina produzidos no hipotálamo.

## Adrenal

- **Córtex**: mesoderma. **Medula**: crista neural (**células cromafins**).
- De fora para dentro: **glomerulosa** (aldosterona), **fasciculada** (cortisol), **reticular** (andrógenos).
- A glomerulosa responde principalmente à **angiotensina II** e ao **potássio**; a fasciculada e a reticular dependem do **ACTH**.
- O cortisol chega à medula por um fluxo portal local e ajuda a produção de **epinefrina**.
- Veias: a veia adrenal **direita** drena direto na **VCI**; a **esquerda** drena na **veia renal esquerda**.

## Pâncreas endócrino

- **Alfa**: glucagon. **Beta**: insulina (as mais numerosas). **Delta**: somatostatina. **Células PP**: polipeptídeo pancreático.

## Cirurgia da tireoide

- **Nervo laríngeo recorrente**: perto da **artéria tireóidea inferior**; a lesão causa **rouquidão** e prega vocal imóvel.
- **Ramo externo do nervo laríngeo superior**: acompanha a **artéria tireóidea superior**; a lesão enfraquece o **cricotireóideo** e a voz aguda.
- A retirada ou desvascularização das paratireoides pode causar **hipocalcemia**.
